Hi Jared / team —

Following up on the technical asks: short answers here and we’ll cover the rest in the deep-dive.

- SOC 2 scope: Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II covers our hosted control plane and core inference runtime when run in Redwood-managed infrastructure. For Redwood Private (customer VPC + control plane), our SOC 2 scope documents the control plane’s operational controls; customer VPC network controls remain in the customer boundary. We can provide a bridge letter summarizing what controls apply and which are customer responsibilities. (See attached SOC2-summary-2025.pdf)

- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS CMKs (bring-your-own-key) for cloud VPC deployments; there’s a documented integration flow that Mina will share in the deep-dive. For on-prem air-gapped packages, we support PKCS#11 HSM integrations; we’ll need to validate model artifact signing and key escrow procedures during the design.

- Network isolation & ingress/egress: Typical deployment options we recommend:
  * Customer VPC with private subnets + VPC endpoints to Redwood control plane (no public ingress to nodes).
  * Transit gateway or direct connect for private connectivity to Redwood control plane in our regions.
  * Air-gapped: full on-prem bundle, no outbound connections; artifacts transferred via signed media under M-of-N ops procedures.

- Data flow for PHI: We can run inference without persisting request payloads to disk and with strict KV-cache TTLs; audit logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM over a secure private link.

I’ll bring an internal checklist and the KMS integration draft to the session. If you can share any network diagrams (firewalls, proxies) we’ll pre-annotate them.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
